notes:
Passed on the fake backend (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). Model-authored and unreviewed; no hardware was attached and no hardware run was made. One device class is implemented: the card's first entry symbol, multiworld.envs.gridworlds.goal_gridworld:GoalGridworld registered as GoalGridworld-v0. The other four card entry symbols (SawyerPushAndReachXYEasyEnv, SawyerDoorHookEnv, SawyerPickAndPlaceEnvYZ, SawyerReachXYEnv) and the card's MuJoCo XML models are not covered: they need mujoco-py and the MuJoCo 2.1 binaries and are actuated robot arms, not the selected grid world. The upstream is legacy Gym, not gymnasium: reset() takes no seed and step() returns a four-tuple, which GymnasiumBridge accepts; the class remains a GymnasiumDriver card match. The fake is a pure Python re-implementation of GoalGridworld and was not compared with the upstream environment: it seeds Python's random.Random from reset(seed) while upstream draws from the unseeded global numpy generator, and it has no rendering. The real observation size (10 x 10 x 1 flattened to 100 floats) is kept; no array is omitted. The fidelity contract is F0, timestep 0 (event-driven grid model), realtime_factor 0, clock lockstep, reset full, no snapshot/restore, with four gaps. No Limits are declared by the driver: action.index 0 to 4 is derived from the environment's Discrete(5) action space, and ticks is bounded by the family max_ticks setting. Two expected family-driver warnings remain: G6.NO_NATIVE_CALL for cap.world.seed.v1 (the seed only affects the next reset) and four G8.NO_UNIT for the integer inputs the bridge derives (ticks, action.index and seed twice), listed in PLAYBOOK.md section 8. Only catalogue classes cap.world.step/reset/seed.v1 are used, so there are no catalogue requests. gate.digest is the digest the check printed; check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run.
